::: {.patient-banner}
## Augmentative & Alternative Communication (AAC) Consultation

Today's simulation focuses on evaluating communication barriers and implementing augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) strategies in the acute care setting.

Students will review four patient consultations, identify barriers to functional communication, evaluate potential access methods, and select appropriate communication supports.

Throughout the simulation, emphasis will be placed on patient-centered care, clinical reasoning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and establishing reliable communication for immediate medical and personal needs.
:::

::: {.warning}
## SLP Task

You are the speech-language pathologist responding to AAC consultations for four patients experiencing different communication barriers in the acute care setting.

For each patient, review the available clinical information, identify communication strengths and limitations, and determine appropriate AAC strategies to trial.

Consider how motor abilities, vision, hearing, cognition, language, medical status, and environmental factors may influence communication access.

Develop recommendations that support the patient's ability to communicate immediate needs, participate in medical care, and interact with family and healthcare providers.
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, students will be able to:

- Identify barriers to functional communication in the acute care setting.
- Evaluate communication abilities and access methods, including motor, visual, auditory, cognitive, and linguistic factors.
- Differentiate low-tech and high-tech AAC approaches based on patient presentation.
- Select and trial individualized AAC strategies to support immediate communication needs.
- Adapt communication approaches based on patient abilities, environmental barriers, and available resources.
- Demonstrate patient-centered communication and education regarding AAC use.
- Develop recommendations for interdisciplinary implementation and follow-up.
- Communicate clinical findings and recommendations through professional documentation.

---

## Today's Modules

### 1. Case A: Quadriplegia & Loss of Speech

Evaluate communication access for a patient with quadriplegia who is unable to communicate verbally and has limited voluntary movement.

Consider alternative access methods, including eye gaze, partner-assisted scanning, and other appropriate AAC supports.

[Begin Case A](case-a.html)

### 2. Case B: Visual Impairment & Pain

Evaluate a patient experiencing pain and difficulty communicating immediate needs without access to their glasses.

Consider how visual limitations, positioning, and discomfort may affect communication access and the selection of AAC strategies.

[Begin Case B](case-b.html)

### 3. Case C: Spanish-Speaking Patient

Evaluate communication needs for a patient whose preferred language is Spanish.

Consider language access, culturally and linguistically appropriate communication supports, and collaboration with qualified medical interpreters.

[Begin Case C](case-c.html)

### 4. Case D: Hearing Impairment

Evaluate communication barriers for a patient who does not have access to their hearing aids.

Consider how hearing loss may influence communication with medical staff and identify appropriate strategies to support comprehension and participation.

[Begin Case D](case-d.html)

### 5. AAC Resources & Clinical Considerations

Review AAC assessment considerations, communication access methods, and strategies for supporting patient communication in acute care.

Use these resources to inform clinical decisions and recommendations throughout the simulation.

[Review AAC Resources](resources.html)
